title: Create D-Optimal Mixture Design
selectedvars: Select mixture components (2+ numeric columns from the active dataset)
lblComponentNote: The active dataset should have exactly 2 rows for the selected component columns: row 1 = lower bound, row 2 = upper bound for each component, expressed in the SAME units as 'Total amount' below. If every component can range freely from 0 to Total, set row 1 = 0 and row 2 = Total for all components -- but for a simple unconstrained mixture, Create Mixture Design (Simplex Lattice/Centroid) is usually a better and faster choice than this dialog.
totalAmount: Total amount (components should sum to this value)
candidateLevels: Candidate grid resolution (levels per component axis)
candidateLevelsHelp: Controls how finely the feasible mixture region is discretized before the D-optimal search runs. Higher values give the search more candidate points to choose from (better designs) but take longer and use more memory. Use an ODD value (default: 11) so the candidate grid can represent an exact 50/50 binary blend (both components at Total/2, e.g. 50 when Total=100, 0.5 when Total=1) -- an even value cannot include that exact halfway point, forcing the search to approximate binary blends with the nearest available fraction instead. If you see a 'not enough feasible candidate points' error, increase this value (keeping it odd).
formula: Model formula (leave blank for a default quadratic Scheffé model in all selected components)
lbl1: You may not need to change the randomization settings

help.title: Create D-Optimal Mixture Design
help.r_help: help(gen.mixture, package = AlgDesign); help(Dopt.design, package = DoE.wrapper)
help.body:
Description
Creates a D-optimal design for a mixture experiment where individual components have their own lower/upper bound constraints in addition to the overall sum-to-Total requirement. Use this dialog instead of Create Mixture Design when your constrained mixture region is too irregular for a standard Simplex Lattice / Simplex Centroid / Extreme Vertices design, or when you need an exact run count that doesn't match a standard design's natural size.

How it works
  • A fine candidate grid of feasible mixture points (all combinations summing to the Total, filtered to respect every component's lower/upper bound) is generated first.
  • A D-optimal subset of the requested size is then selected from that candidate grid using the Federov exchange algorithm, for the specified model formula.
Preparing your data
Before opening this dialog, create a small table with one column per mixture component and exactly two rows: row 1 = lower bound, row 2 = upper bound, in the same units as Total amount (e.g., percentages if Total = 100).

Model formula
Mixture models never include an intercept, since the components already sum to a constant. Left blank, this dialog uses a default quadratic Scheffé model equivalent to ~ -1 + (Comp1 + Comp2 + ... )^2 — main effects plus all pairwise component interactions. Type your own formula (e.g., ~ -1 + Comp1 + Comp2 + Comp3 for a linear-only mixture model) to override this default.

Use an ODD candidate grid resolution
The candidate grid places points at fractions k/(resolution−1) of the Total, for every integer k from 0 to resolution−1. An exact 50/50 binary blend — both components at Total/2 (e.g. 50 when Total=100, 0.5 when Total=1) — the point almost every quadratic Scheffé model wants at each pair of components, is only present in that grid when (resolution−1) is even, i.e. when resolution itself is odd. With an even resolution, Total/2 is simply absent from the candidate set, and the search silently substitutes the nearest available fraction instead (e.g. 55.56/44.44 rather than 50/50, if Total = 100). The default resolution of 11 avoids this; if you change it, keep it odd. A NOTE is printed automatically if an even resolution is used.

If you see “not enough feasible candidate points”
Increase the Candidate grid resolution (keeping it odd), or relax one or more component bounds — the requested run count exceeds the number of distinct feasible points found within the specified bounds at the current grid resolution.

Requires the 'AlgDesign' R package (for candidate generation and the D-optimal search) and 'DoE.wrapper' (already used elsewhere in the DOE menu).
